metadata.dataset: Striver SDE Sheet — original metadata/test data
metadata.note: Batch 1 contains 50 SDE-sheet-aligned problems. Descriptions and hints are newly written; third-party editorial/problem text is not reproduced.

problem.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problem.description: Modify a matrix so that every row and column containing a zero becomes entirely zero, while preserving the required in-place constraint.
hints: First identify which rows and columns must be cleared.
Avoid changing cells to zero too early because that can create new markers.
Can the first row and first column act as marker storage?

problem.title: Pascal's Triangle
problem.description: Generate the first numRows rows of Pascal's triangle.
hints: Every row starts and ends with 1.
An interior value comes from the two values directly above it.
Build each row from the previous row.

problem.title: Next Permutation
problem.description: Transform an integer sequence into its next lexicographically greater permutation. If it is already the largest permutation, return the smallest ordering.
hints: Scan from the right to find the first increasing pair.
Swap the pivot with the smallest larger value on its right.
Reverse the suffix after the pivot.

problem.title: Kadane's Algorithm
problem.description: Find the maximum possible sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
hints: Maintain the best sum ending at the current position.
A negative running sum is usually better discarded.
Keep a separate global maximum.

problem.title: Sort an Array of 0s, 1s and 2s
problem.description: Sort an array containing only 0, 1 and 2 in-place.
hints: Maintain regions for 0s, unknown values and 2s.
A 0 belongs on the left; a 2 belongs on the right.
Do not advance the middle pointer after swapping an unknown value with the right side.

problem.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problem.description: Choose one buying day followed by a later selling day to maximize profit.
hints: Track the cheapest price seen so far.
At each day calculate the profit from selling today.
Return zero if no profitable transaction exists.

problem.title: Rotate Matrix
problem.description: Rotate a square matrix 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
hints: Transpose the matrix first.
Then reverse every row.
Both operations can be done without another matrix.

problem.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
problem.description: Merge all overlapping closed intervals and return the resulting non-overlapping intervals.
hints: Sort intervals by starting point.
Compare each interval with the last merged interval.
Extend the end when they overlap.

problem.title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays Without Extra Space
problem.description: Given two sorted arrays, rearrange them in-place so their combined values remain sorted, with the first array holding the smaller values.
hints: Think of the two arrays as one virtual sorted array.
Compare elements separated by a shrinking gap.
Swap values that are out of order.

problem.title: Find Duplicate in Array
problem.description: An array contains n+1 integers in the range 1..n. Find the repeated value without modifying the array.
hints: Treat each value as a pointer to another index.
A duplicate creates a cycle.
Use Floyd's tortoise-and-hare technique.
constraints: Exactly one value is repeated at least twice

problem.title: Repeat and Missing Number
problem.description: An array contains every value from 1..n except one missing value, while another value occurs twice. Find both.
hints: XOR all expected and observed values to isolate two candidates.
Separate numbers by a distinguishing bit.
Check which candidate is duplicated to identify the missing value.
constraints: Exactly one missing and one repeated value

problem.title: Count Inversions
problem.description: Count pairs of indices i < j for which the value at i is greater than the value at j.
hints: A merge step can count cross-half inversions efficiently.
When a right-half value is chosen before remaining left-half values, all those left values form inversions.
Use a 64-bit counter for the answer.

problem.title: Search in a 2D Matrix
problem.description: Search for a target in a matrix whose rows are sorted and whose row ranges are ordered globally.
hints: Treat the matrix as a flattened sorted array.
Map a flat index back to row and column.
Binary search gives logarithmic search time.

problem.title: Pow(x, n)
problem.description: Compute x raised to an integer exponent n, including negative exponents.
hints: Exponentiation by squaring reduces the number of multiplications.
Handle negative exponents carefully.
Use a wider integer type for the exponent when needed.

problem.title: Majority Element
problem.description: Find the value that appears more than half of the array length.
hints: Keep a candidate and a counter.
Equal values increase support; different values decrease it.
The majority element survives cancellation.

problem.title: Majority Element II
problem.description: Return all values that occur more than floor(n/3) times.
hints: There can be at most two such values.
Maintain two candidates and their counters.
Perform a final counting pass to verify candidates.

problem.title: Grid Unique Paths
problem.description: Count paths from the top-left to bottom-right of an m by n grid when movement is only right or down.
hints: Each cell can be reached from its top or left neighbor.
A 1D DP array is enough.
For larger values, consider a combinatorial formulation.

problem.title: Reverse Pairs
problem.description: Count index pairs where an earlier value is more than twice a later value.
hints: Count qualifying pairs before merging the two sorted halves.
Use two pointers for the cross-half count.
Then perform the normal merge.

problem.title: Two Sum
problem.description: Return indices of two distinct elements whose values add to a target.
hints: Store previously seen values in a hash map.
For the current value, look for target minus that value.
Return the matching pair as soon as it is found.

problem.title: 4 Sum
problem.description: Return all unique quadruplets whose four values add to a target.
hints: Sort first.
Fix two positions and solve the remaining two-sum problem with two pointers.
Skip equal values at every level to avoid duplicates.

problem.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problem.description: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integers in an unsorted array.
hints: A number starts a sequence only if its predecessor is absent.
Then walk forward until the sequence ends.
A hash set gives average constant-time membership checks.

problem.title: Largest Subarray with Sum 0
problem.description: Find the maximum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is zero.
hints: Track prefix sums.
If the same prefix sum appears twice, the values between those positions sum to zero.
Keep the earliest index for each prefix sum.

problem.title: Count Subarrays with XOR K
problem.description: Count contiguous subarrays whose bitwise XOR equals a given value K.
hints: Let prefixXor be the XOR up to the current index.
A previous prefix equal to prefixXor XOR K forms a valid subarray.
Store frequencies, not just first positions.

problem.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problem.description: Find the length of the longest substring containing no repeated character.
hints: Use a moving left boundary.
When a character repeats, move the left boundary past its previous occurrence.
Store last-seen positions.

problem.title: Reverse a Linked List
problem.description: Reverse a singly linked list and return its new head.
hints: Keep previous, current and next references.
Save next before changing current.next.
Move all three references forward.

problem.title: Middle of Linked List
problem.description: Return the middle node of a singly linked list; for an even length, return the second middle.
hints: Move one pointer one step and another two steps.
When the fast pointer reaches the end, the slow pointer is at the answer.

problem.title: Merge Two Sorted Linked Lists
problem.description: Merge two ascending singly linked lists into one ascending list.
hints: Use a dummy node to simplify the head case.
Always attach the smaller current node.
Attach the remaining suffix at the end.

problem.title: Remove Nth Node from End
problem.description: Remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list and return the head.
hints: Place two pointers n nodes apart.
Advance them together until the leading pointer reaches the end.
A dummy node handles removal of the original head.

problem.title: Delete a Node with O(1) Extra Space
problem.description: Delete a given non-tail node when only that node is provided, without access to the list head.
hints: Copy the successor's value into the given node.
Then bypass the successor.
The supplied node is guaranteed not to be the tail.
constraints: Given node is not the tail

problem.title: Add Two Numbers as Linked Lists
problem.description: Add two non-negative integers represented by linked lists with least significant digits first.
hints: Process both lists while either remains or a carry exists.
Create one result digit per step.
Carry can be appended as a final node.

problem.title: Intersection Point of Two Linked Lists
problem.description: Find the first node shared by two singly linked lists, or report that they do not intersect.
hints: After reaching the end, switch each pointer to the other head.
Both pointers then traverse equal total lengths.
Reference identity, not node value, determines intersection.

testCases.input: A=[4,1,8,4,5], B=[5,6,1,8,4,5], shared starts at value 8

problem.title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
problem.description: Determine whether a singly linked list contains a cycle.
hints: Move slow one step and fast two steps.
If they meet, a cycle exists.
If fast reaches null, there is no cycle.

problem.title: Reverse Nodes in Groups of K
problem.description: Reverse nodes in consecutive groups of size k. Leave a final group unchanged if it has fewer than k nodes.
hints: Check that a complete group exists before reversing.
Reverse exactly k links.
Connect the reversed group to the next group.

problem.title: Palindrome Linked List
problem.description: Determine whether a singly linked list reads the same forward and backward.
hints: Find the midpoint.
Reverse the second half.
Compare the two halves node by node.

problem.title: Starting Point of Linked List Cycle
problem.description: Return the first node belonging to a cycle, or null when no cycle exists.
hints: First detect a meeting point using slow and fast pointers.
Reset one pointer to the head.
Move both one step; their next meeting point is the cycle entry.

problem.title: Flatten a Linked List
problem.description: Flatten a linked structure where each node has a next pointer and a sorted child list, producing one sorted child chain.
hints: Flatten the remaining lists recursively.
Merge two sorted child chains.
Use the child pointer for the flattened chain.

problem.title: Rotate Linked List
problem.description: Rotate a singly linked list to the right by k positions.
hints: Compute the length and reduce k modulo the length.
Connect the tail to the head temporarily.
Break the circle at the correct predecessor.

problem.title: Clone Linked List with Random Pointer
problem.description: Create a deep copy of a linked list where each node has next and random references.
hints: One approach maps each original node to its clone.
An O(1)-extra-space approach interleaves clones with originals.
Restore the original list after assigning random links.

problem.title: 3 Sum
problem.description: Return all unique triples whose values sum to zero.
hints: Sort the array.
Fix one value and solve two-sum on the suffix.
Skip duplicate values for unique triples.

problem.title: Trapping Rain Water
problem.description: Compute how much water can be trapped between vertical bars after rainfall.
hints: Water at a position depends on the smaller of the best left and right boundaries.
Two pointers can avoid storing both prefix arrays.
Always advance the side with the smaller boundary.

problem.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problem.description: Remove duplicates from a sorted array in-place so each distinct value appears once, returning the number of retained values.
hints: Use a slow pointer for the next unique position.
Scan with a fast pointer.
Write a value only when it differs from the previous retained value.

problem.title: Max Consecutive Ones
problem.description: Find the longest contiguous run of 1s in a binary array.
hints: Maintain the current run length.
Reset it when a zero appears.
Track the maximum seen.

problem.title: N Meetings in One Room
problem.description: Select the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings that can be held in one room.
hints: Sort meetings by finishing time.
Always select the next meeting whose start is after the last selected finish.
The earliest finishing compatible meeting leaves the most room for future meetings.

problem.title: Minimum Number of Platforms
problem.description: Find the minimum number of railway platforms needed so that no train waits, given arrival and departure times.
hints: Sort arrival and departure times separately.
A new arrival before the next departure needs another platform.
A departure first frees a platform.

problem.title: Job Sequencing Problem
problem.description: Given jobs with deadlines and profits, schedule at most one job per time slot to maximize total profit.
hints: Sort jobs by decreasing profit.
Try to place each job in the latest available slot before its deadline.
Use a slot structure to find free positions efficiently.

expectedComplexity.time: O(n log n) with efficient slots

problem.title: Fractional Knapsack
problem.description: Maximize value in a knapsack of fixed capacity when fractions of items may be taken.
hints: Compute value per unit weight.
Take higher-ratio items first.
Only the final item may need to be fractional.

problem.title: Minimum Coins
problem.description: Using a supplied set of standard coin denominations, find the minimum number of coins needed to make a target amount.
hints: Take the largest denomination that does not exceed the remaining amount.
Repeat until the amount becomes zero.
This greedy rule is valid for canonical denominations such as standard Indian/decimal coin sets, but not for arbitrary denominations.

problem.title: Activity Selection
problem.description: Select the maximum number of mutually compatible activities when each activity has a start and finish time.
hints: This is equivalent to choosing meetings by earliest finishing time.
Sort by finish time and greedily accept compatible activities.
Do not sort by duration.

problem.title: Subset Sum
problem.description: Determine whether some subset of the given non-negative integers has sum exactly equal to a target.
hints: For each value, consider taking or skipping it.
Memoization removes repeated states.
A boolean DP indexed by sum works when the target is manageable.

problem.title: Subset Sum II
problem.description: Generate all unique subsets of an integer array that may contain duplicates.
hints: Sort first so equal values become adjacent.
At the same recursion depth, skip duplicate values.
A chosen duplicate at a deeper depth is still allowed.
